note: Re-judged 2026-10-30 by an independent auditor (authored none of the userns spec commits d8427e4380, b00e3c6710, 68b723ec4f, 7d11a51269). userns.Enter (internal/test/userns/userns_linux.go) re-executes the one test in a new user+net+mount namespace and returns false in the parent only after the child's own PASS line; a child failure, a zero-exit failure or a child that selected nothing fails the parent, and a child skip skips it, so the guard cannot turn a red into a green. Section 4.4: "Support for receiving and sending IP multicast datagrams, along with the appropriate lower-level protocol support, is required." TestOSPFTransportVethMulticastRoundTrip and TestOSPFTransportAllDRoutersReceive changed by the guard and by the CAP_NET_RAW probe failing instead of skipping (stronger); withVethPair's namespace/veth refusals likewise fail now. Bodies otherwise unchanged: the round trip reads IP_MULTICAST_IF and TTL 1, sends AllSPFRouters across a veth into a peer namespace and asserts receiving interface, source and exact payload; AllDRouters is received after join (positive control) and not received after leave. The namespace the lab builds now sits inside the child's own network namespace, which removes host-route and host-rp_filter influence without changing any assertion. Proves Ze's socket/send/receive boundary, not Linux forwarding (not required). Records (setMulticastOptions, leaveGroup reverts) current.
